task: W2-81 (DAEO-l78m) batch 4: fix the ten review findings in the suite only, each with a self-test that failed on the batch-3 head and passes now.
status: DONE. Committed as `0a2608e40388`; the whole suite passes 183 of 183, alone and with `-n auto`.
work_completed: All ten behaviours are fixed (details below). No existing expectation was lowered, with one correction to an old case: the reviewed-rename case now writes its rename target with the built content, because the new rule requires the target to hold the file as built.
files_changed: All under `tests/acceptance/W2-81/`.
- New: `test_w2_81_review.py`.
- Changed: `w2_81_judge.py`, `w2_81_standin.py`, `w2_81_build.py`, `w2_81_run.py`, `test_w2_81_judge.py`, `README.md`.
evidence:

- **Why some failed on the head:** most failed on the judged status or on what was shown. A few failed partly for other reasons:

| Run | Result | Time (pytest) | Wall |

`test_w2_81_review.py` alone: 43 passed. Collect-only over `tests`, last line: `18723/18725 tests collected (2 deselected) in 12.65s`.

discoveries:
1. **Several secrets of one form.** Each planted secret is now checked against its own value, drawn again from the seed and its salt (`judge.own_value`), so two secrets of one form are told apart. A leak of either one is MISHANDLED under its own id, and the other is not blamed. Test: `test_each_secret_of_one_form_is_checked_against_its_own_value`, a second forge token added as a variant to the TypeScript repository, each value leaked into a record, the index and a log (6 cases).
2. **Hidden files that cannot be read.**
   - The runner refuses a variants file or hidden question set that cannot be read, or is not of its form, naming the file only.
   - The hook wraps each variant: any failure becomes `hidden variant #<n> (<id>) cannot be built`, and its secret checks no longer name paths.
   - The command catches these, prints `refused: …` and exits 2.
   - Tests: `test_the_variants_hook_names_a_variant_by_number_and_id_only` (4 cases) and `test_a_hidden_file_that_cannot_be_read_is_refused_naming_the_file_only` (4 cases through the command, checking its output and any report or log).
3. **An orphaned test kept from running.** The rule no longer depends on a list of skip forms. The test file must have the build's exact content (a git blob id compare), and no test-runner configuration file in its folder or above may be new, changed or gone. Test: `test_an_orphaned_test_kept_from_running_or_collected_is_mishandled`, 9 forms:
   - Python: an import skip, an expected-failure mark, a rename out of collection, `collect_ignore` in a new conftest;
   - TypeScript: `xtest`, `xdescribe`, `test.todo`;
   - Rust: `cfg(any())` on the file, and on the test.
4. **Planted files held as built.**
   - Every file a planted problem's handling depends on must keep the build's content and place. It may leave only by a MOVE or RENAME in A3 whose path map A5 reviewed, with the target holding it as built, and only where its kind allows that. A legacy document to retire may also leave by a reviewed RETIRE.
   - The stand-in copies are now `git clone --shared` of the built repository, so the judge can read the build's HEAD in them.
   - The runner's `follow_moves` keeps a moved stale spec forbidden at its new place, and moves a gold source with its file.
   - **Deletion reviewed at A5:** it stays MISHANDLED, as before. The README says that call is the owner's.
   - Tests: `test_a_planted_file_moved_deleted_or_rewritten_on_its_own_is_mishandled` (8 cases), and `test_a_stale_spec_moved_by_a_reviewed_action_stays_handled_and_forbidden_at_its_new_place`.
5. **A value in the adoption's own commits.** The judge now reads every object the adoption added after the build's HEAD, on any ref or reflog, for each planted value. A history it cannot read rules nothing out. Tests: `test_a_value_committed_and_removed_by_the_adoption_is_mishandled` (on `main`, and on another ref) and `test_an_adopted_repository_whose_history_cannot_be_read_rules_nothing_out`.
6. **A control out of the index.** A control is FLAGGED when it is left out of a readable index, mapped to no namespace the path map holds, or changed in place. Test: `test_a_control_out_of_the_index_or_mapped_nowhere_is_flagged`.
7. **The successor plan classed superseded** is MISHANDLED. Test: `test_the_successor_plan_classed_superseded_too_is_mishandled`.
8. **The verdict while the secret is open.** Any verdict other than NOT_ADOPTED_HEALTHY with the secret's finding open is MISHANDLED. The owner's acceptance by name (CAP-44.h) has no record today, so it is NOT_BUILT and not read; the README says so. Test: `test_any_verdict_but_not_adopted_healthy_with_the_secret_open_is_mishandled`.
9. **Two builds sharing one manifests folder.** A build refuses a manifests folder that already holds manifests. `run.json` now records each repository's head, and read mode refuses a manifest whose seed or head is not the run's, naming the repository. Tests: `test_a_build_refuses_a_manifests_folder_that_holds_manifests` and `test_read_mode_refuses_manifests_that_are_not_the_runs`.
10. **The budget clause.** "Within the budget" is now stated as not measured today: no budget is stated in the path map's schema, in `gov rebuild`'s records or in the Contract. Each judgement lists it under `not_measured`, and the README's earlier promise to measure it is removed. Test: `test_the_large_files_budget_clause_is_said_to_be_not_measured`.
risks:
- **Item 6 on the real run.** Today's `gov` indexes only governance namespaces lexically, so a control that is product code will be FLAGGED as left out of the index unless the adoption's path map indexes it. The real run may show this as a finding about the index, not about the adoption's judgement.
- **Item 3's configuration list.** The list of test-runner configuration file names is the one part of item 3 that depends on a list.
lessons:
- **Guard refusals:** none.
- **A slip I made:** one command used a here-document, which the command-form rules forbid. It ran a no-op and wrote nothing. I didn't repeat it.
- **Retrieval:** not used, as you directed.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: Two calls are left with the owner: whether a deletion reviewed at A5 may count as handled (kept as MISHANDLED for now), and the form of the owner's acceptance record for the lite verdict (NOT_BUILT until W2-52).
recommended_next_action: The orchestrator re-runs the independent review on `0a2608e40388`; the first real run follows after blocks B and C.
